question: A team moves its live pricing sheet into a project's knowledge so every chat in the project can use it, and then changes its prices two months later. What is the greatest risk?
options: A) The pricing sheet will be counted twice, once as knowledge and once in each conversation.
B) Every chat in that project will keep quoting the superseded prices with complete confidence.
C) Colleagues outside the project will be unable to see the pricing sheet in their own chats.
D) The project will refuse any further uploads until the outdated pricing sheet has been removed.
correct_answers: B) Every chat in that project will keep quoting the superseded prices with complete confidence.
explanations: Incorrect. Nothing is double-counted in that way, and this does not describe a real failure mode.
Correct. Making knowledge durable also makes staleness durable. Until the sheet is replaced, the project answers confidently from a document that no longer reflects reality.
Incorrect. That is the expected scope of a project rather than a risk created by the price change.
Incorrect. There is no such block, and framing this as an upload problem misses where the damage actually occurs.
